workflow_contract.queue_mode: GitHub default: at most one pending run; a newer pending run replaces the previous pending run
workflow_contract.credential: Read-only GitHub App installation token scoped to the controlled source and consumer repositories

runs.reason: The run was pending behind v1.2.0 and was replaced by the newer v1.4.0 pending run.

interpretation.safe_condition: Every queued execution performs a state-based full scan and computes desired updates from current repository and release state. Event payload order is not used as correctness state.
interpretation.unsafe_condition: Coalescing is not safe for event-specific side effects, counters, destructive operations, or routing that requires every individual payload to be processed.
interpretation.result: For state-reconciliation full scans, one running plus one latest pending execution converged to the newest released version while avoiding a redundant intermediate Renovate run.

limitations: The experiment used one controlled consumer, not a large full fleet; EXP-0021 separately covers full-scan scaling.
The three temporary tags pointed to the same source commit because the test variable was release identity and queue semantics, not source content changes.
The workflow used workflow_dispatch to create controlled events. A production repository_dispatch trigger must preserve the same state-based full-scan behavior.
The result does not apply if future processing introduces mandatory per-event side effects.
